knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9,
                      fig.height = 5, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)
source("case-helpers.R")
source("anim.R")
pfmt <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", fmt(p, 3))
```

# Calls and text messages in the Copenhagen Networks Study

The Copenhagen Networks Study gave smartphones to about 700 first-year
university students in Copenhagen and recorded, among other channels, their
phone calls and text messages over four weeks (Sapiezynski et al. 2019).
`copenhagen_calls` and `copenhagen_sms` are two relational event logs on the
same students, and `copenhagen_actors` records each student's gender. The two
logs are two layers of one multiplex network: the same pair can call, text, or
both. This case study asks whether a pair's history in one layer changes its
rate in the other, how reciprocity and repetition act within each layer,
whether students call and text within their own gender more than by chance,
and how both layers follow the clock.

## The two layers

```{r data}
data(copenhagen_calls); data(copenhagen_sms); data(copenhagen_actors)
calls <- copenhagen_calls[, c("sender", "receiver", "time", "duration")]
sms   <- copenhagen_sms[,   c("sender", "receiver", "time")]
fem   <- setNames(copenhagen_actors$female, copenhagen_actors$id)

pair <- function(d) paste(pmin(d$sender, d$receiver), pmax(d$sender, d$receiver))
pc <- table(pair(calls)); ps <- table(pair(sms))
both <- intersect(names(pc), names(ps))
data.frame(layer = c("calls", "text messages"),
           events = c(nrow(calls), nrow(sms)),
           students = c(length(unique(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver))),
                        length(unique(c(sms$sender, sms$receiver)))),
           pairs = c(length(pc), length(ps)),
           pairs_in_both_layers = length(both))
```

```{r layer-numbers, include = FALSE}
share_calls_both <- sum(pc[both]) / sum(pc)
share_sms_both   <- sum(ps[both]) / sum(ps)
missed <- mean(calls$duration == -1)
```

`r fmt(length(both))` pairs appear in both layers. They carry
`r pct(share_calls_both)` of all calls and `r pct(share_sms_both)` of all text
messages, so most communication runs through pairs that use both channels.
A call is recorded whether or not it was answered (`r pct(missed)` have
duration `-1`, the release's code for a missed call); every call attempt is an
event here. Gender is recorded for
`r pct(mean(unique(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver, sms$sender, sms$receiver)) %in% names(fem)))`
of the students who appear in either log.

```{r layers-figure, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.2, fig.alt = "Three panels with the same student positions: pairs that call and text, pairs that only text, pairs that only call"}
# one layout for both layers: the union of the two networks, largest component
u <- rbind(data.frame(from = calls$sender, to = calls$receiver),
           data.frame(from = sms$sender, to = sms$receiver))
u <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(u))), u, sum)
g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(u[, 1:2], directed = FALSE)
comp <- igraph::components(g)
giant <- names(comp$membership)[comp$membership == which.max(comp$csize)]
lay <- layout_graph(u[u$from %in% giant & u$to %in% giant, ], ids = giant, seed = 3)

gcol <- c(female = pal[5], male = pal[4], unknown = "#B4BBC0")
g_of <- function(id) ifelse(is.na(fem[id]), "unknown", ifelse(fem[id] == 1, "female", "male"))
lcol <- c("calls and texts" = ink, "texts only" = pal[2], "calls only" = pal[6])
e <- data.frame(pair = union(names(pc), names(ps)))
e$calls <- as.numeric(pc[e$pair]); e$texts <- as.numeric(ps[e$pair])
e$calls[is.na(e$calls)] <- 0; e$texts[is.na(e$texts)] <- 0
ab <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(e$pair, " ")); e$from <- ab[, 1]; e$to <- ab[, 2]
e <- e[e$from %in% lay$id & e$to %in% lay$id, ]
e$layer <- ifelse(e$calls > 0 & e$texts > 0, "calls and texts", ifelse(e$texts > 0, "texts only", "calls only"))
e$w <- pmax(e$calls + e$texts, 4); e$col <- lcol[e$layer]   # pairs with 4 or fewer events share the thinnest visible line
act <- table(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver, sms$sender, sms$receiver))
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),
                    col = gcol[g_of(lay$id)])
# a pair is "peripheral" when one of its students has no other partner in either layer
deg <- table(c(e$from, e$to))
e$leaf <- deg[e$from] == 1 | deg[e$to] == 1
nodes$col <- "#8C969D"
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 3.2, 0.1), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (L in names(lcol)) {
  k <- e$layer == L
  # draw_network scales widths to the panel's largest pair; rescale so all panels share one scale
  ml <- 3.4 * (log1p(max(e$w[k])) / log1p(max(e$w)))^1.4
  bg <- e[, c("from", "to")]; bg$w <- 1; bg$col <- "#DCE0E3"      # the whole network, faint, behind each panel
  draw_network(transform(nodes, col = "#E6E9EB"), bg, directed = FALSE, max_lwd = 0.4,
               node_scale = c(0.35, 1.8), xlim = c(-0.02, 1.02), ylim = c(-0.02, max(nodes$y) + 0.02))
  draw_network(nodes[nodes$id %in% c(e$from[k], e$to[k]), ], e[k, c("from", "to", "w", "col")],
               directed = FALSE, max_lwd = ml, node_scale = c(0.35, 1.8), add = TRUE)
  title_left(sprintf("%s: %s pairs", L, fmt(sum(k))),
             sprintf("%s end at a student with no other partner", pct(mean(e$leaf[k]), 0)))
}
mtext("All three kinds of pair run through the same network", side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5, adj = 0.01, cex = 0.95, font = 2, col = ink)
mtext(sprintf("Same %s students at the same positions in every panel; grey: the whole network; line width: calls + texts, one scale for all panels",
              fmt(length(giant))), side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = -1.2, cex = 0.68, col = ink_soft)
par(op)
nl <- table(factor(e$layer, levels = names(lcol)))
leaf_share <- tapply(e$leaf, factor(e$layer, levels = names(lcol)), mean)
```

The figure draws the `r fmt(length(giant))` students of the largest connected
group of the two layers together (out of
`r fmt(length(unique(c(u$from, u$to))))`) at the same positions in three
panels: pairs that both call and text, pairs that only text, and pairs that
only call. Line width is calls plus texts (pairs with four or fewer events are
drawn alike) and dot size the student's events. The
`r fmt(nl[["calls and texts"]])` two-channel pairs span the whole network;
`r pct(leaf_share[["calls and texts"]], 0)` of them end at a student with no
other partner, against `r pct(leaf_share[["texts only"]], 0)` of the
text-only and `r pct(leaf_share[["calls only"]], 0)` of the call-only pairs.

```{r overlap-figure, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 6, out.width = "70%", fig.align = "center", fig.alt = "Calls against text messages per pair, both on log scales, with pairs that use only one channel on the axes"}
pairs <- union(names(pc), names(ps))
n_call <- as.numeric(pc[pairs]); n_call[is.na(n_call)] <- 0
n_sms  <- as.numeric(ps[pairs]); n_sms[is.na(n_sms)] <- 0
ends <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(pairs, " "))
comp_g <- ifelse(is.na(fem[ends[, 1]]) | is.na(fem[ends[, 2]]), "unknown",
          ifelse(fem[ends[, 1]] == fem[ends[, 2]], "same gender", "mixed gender"))
ccol <- c("same gender" = pal[1], "mixed gender" = pal[6], unknown = "#B4BBC0")
set.seed(4)
jit <- function(n) runif(length(n), -0.12, 0.12)
# every integer column and row gets the same small jitter
x <- log10(n_call + 1) + runif(length(n_call), -0.035, 0.035) + ifelse(n_call == 0, jit(n_call), 0)
y <- log10(n_sms + 1)  + runif(length(n_sms), -0.035, 0.035) + ifelse(n_sms == 0, jit(n_sms), 0)
par(mar = c(4, 4.4, 2.8, 4))
plot(x, y, pch = 21, bg = alpha(ccol[comp_g], 0.55), col = "white", cex = 1.1, lwd = 0.4,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", xlim = c(-0.15, max(x) + 0.1), ylim = c(-0.15, max(y) + 0.1))
at <- c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)
axis(1, at = log10(at + 1), labels = at, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, at = log10(at + 1), labels = at, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("calls between the pair", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.8, col = ink_soft)
mtext("text messages between the pair", side = 2, line = 2.6, cex = 0.8, col = ink_soft)
abline(h = 0.17, v = 0.17, col = rule, lty = 3)
r_both <- cor(log1p(n_call[n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0]), log1p(n_sms[n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0]))
# median texts per bin of calls, pairs using both channels
bb <- n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0; br <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, 200)
bin <- cut(n_call[bb], br, right = FALSE)
med <- tapply(log10(n_sms[bb] + 1), bin, median); mx <- tapply(log10(n_call[bb] + 1), bin, median)
lines(mx, med, col = ink, lwd = 2.2); points(mx, med, pch = 21, bg = ink, col = "white", cex = 1.1)
text(mx[length(mx)], med[length(med)], "median texts\nper calls bin", pos = 4, cex = 0.65, col = ink, xpd = TRUE)
title_left("Pairs that call also text",
           sprintf("n = %s pairs: %s both, %s only text, %s only call (on the axes); r = %.2f (log counts, pairs using both)",
                   fmt(length(pairs)), fmt(sum(n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0)), fmt(sum(n_sms > 0 & n_call == 0)), fmt(sum(n_call > 0 & n_sms == 0)), r_both))
legend("bottomright", legend = names(ccol), pt.bg = ccol, col = "white", pch = 21, pt.cex = 1.3,
       bty = "n", cex = 0.72, text.col = ink)
```

```{r overlap-numbers, include = FALSE}
only_call <- sum(n_call > 0 & n_sms == 0); only_sms <- sum(n_sms > 0 & n_call == 0)
mix <- function(k) mean(comp_g[k] == "mixed gender") / mean(comp_g[k] != "unknown")
mix_sms_only <- mix(n_sms > 0 & n_call == 0); mix_call_any <- mix(n_call > 0)
```

Of the `r fmt(length(pairs))` pairs, `r fmt(length(both))` use both channels,
`r fmt(only_sms)` only text and `r fmt(only_call)` only call. Where a pair uses
both, its call and text counts rise together (correlation of the log counts
`r fmt(r_both, 2)`). Among pairs with known genders,
`r pct(mix_sms_only)` of the text-only pairs are mixed-gender, against
`r pct(mix_call_any)` of the pairs that call.

## Clock time

`time` counts days from the start of the four-week period; the release gives
no calendar date. If the period starts at midnight, `time %% 1` is the time of
day. Both layers fall to their lowest level between 03:00 and 06:00 and peak
in the afternoon and evening, which is what a midnight start implies, but the
release does not state the start, so the clock times below assume one. The weekday of day 1 is not known either, so the weekly
cycle is indexed by the day of the study week (1 to 7), not by weekday names.

```{r clock-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Events per hour across the 28 days, calls and text messages, as day-by-hour heatmaps"}
heat_day_hour <- function(t) {
  m <- table(factor(floor(t), levels = 0:27), factor(floor((t %% 1) * 24), levels = 0:23))
  matrix(as.numeric(m), 28, 24)
}
hc <- heat_day_hour(calls$time); hs <- heat_day_hour(sms$time)
draw_heat <- function(m, col, main, sub) {
  ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", alpha(col, 0.35), col, "#1E2A33"))(64)
  image(0:23 + 0.5, 1:28, t(m), col = ramp, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", useRaster = TRUE,
        xlim = c(0, 24), ylim = c(28.5, 0.5))
  abline(h = seq(7.5, 21.5, 7), col = "white", lwd = 2)
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 24, 6), labels = sprintf("%02d:00", seq(0, 24, 6)), tick = FALSE,
       cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
  axis(2, at = c(1, 8, 15, 22, 28), labels = paste("day", c(1, 8, 15, 22, 28)), las = 1, tick = FALSE,
       cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
  title_left(main, sub)
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2.6, 4.2, 2.8, 1))
draw_heat(hc, pal[1], "Calls per hour", sprintf("darkest cell: %d calls; white lines separate study weeks", max(hc)))
draw_heat(hs, pal[2], "Text messages per hour", sprintf("darkest cell: %d messages", max(hs)))
par(op)
```

```{r clock-numbers, include = FALSE}
night <- function(t) mean(((t %% 1) * 24) >= 2 & ((t %% 1) * 24) < 7)
```

Between 02:00 and 07:00 fall `r pct(night(calls$time))` of the calls and
`r pct(night(sms$time))` of the text messages. Daily totals of the two layers
have correlation `r fmt(cor(rowSums(hc), rowSums(hs)), 2)` over the 28 days.

```{r anim-prep, include = FALSE}
br12 <- seq(0, 28, by = 0.5)                          # 56 half-day windows
lab12 <- sprintf("day %d, %s", floor(head(br12, -1)) + 1, ifelse(head(br12, -1) %% 1 == 0, "00:00-12:00", "12:00-24:00"))
ev <- rbind(data.frame(a = calls$sender, b = calls$receiver, time = calls$time, layer = "call"),
            data.frame(a = sms$sender,   b = sms$receiver,   time = sms$time,   layer = "text"))
win <- findInterval(ev$time, br12)
key <- paste(win, pmin(ev$a, ev$b), pmax(ev$a, ev$b))
both_in_win <- ave(ev$layer == "call", key, FUN = function(z) any(z) && !all(z))
ecol <- ifelse(both_in_win, ink, ifelse(ev$layer == "call", pal[6], pal[2]))
ncol <- setNames(gcol[g_of(unique(c(ev$a, ev$b)))], unique(c(ev$a, ev$b)))
per_win <- tabulate(win, length(br12) - 1)
am <- per_win[seq(1, length(per_win), 2)]; pm <- per_win[seq(2, length(per_win), 2)]
```

```{r anim, echo = FALSE}
anim_events(ev$a, ev$b, ev$time, br12, lab12, node_col = ncol, edge_col = ecol, n_nodes = 120,
            title = "Calls and texts, half a day at a time",
            sub = "120 most active students (pink: female, blue: male); lines: gold calls, purple texts, dark both; grey: the previous windows",
            fps = 4, alt = "The call and text network of the 120 most active students, drawn in 56 half-day windows over the 28 days")
```

The animation steps through the 56 half-day windows on one layout of the 120
most active students. The windows from 12:00 to 24:00 hold
`r pct(sum(pm) / sum(per_win), 0)` of all calls and texts; the busiest window,
`r lab12[which.max(per_win)]`, has `r fmt(max(per_win))` events, and the
quietest of the afternoon-evening windows has `r fmt(min(pm))`.

## A case-control design per layer

Each layer gets its own case-control sample: five non-events per event, dyads
drawn uniformly among the students of that layer (`sample_non_events()` with
`scope = "all"`, `mode = "one"`). All 3,600 calls are cases. For the text
messages, 3,600 of the 24,333 messages are drawn at random (seed 1) as cases,
which keeps the page's build time short; every statistic is still computed
from the full history of both logs, so only the number of strata changes, not
what each stratum compares.

```{r samples}
set.seed(1)
sms_cases <- sms[sort(sample(nrow(sms), nrow(calls))), ]
cc_call <- sample_non_events(calls[, c("sender", "receiver", "time")], n_controls = 5, seed = 1)
cc_sms  <- sample_non_events(sms_cases, n_controls = 5, seed = 1)
c(call_rows = nrow(cc_call), sms_rows = nrow(cc_sms))
```

### Statistics

For a row with sender \(s\), receiver \(r\) at time \(t\), all counts use events
strictly before \(t\):

- **repetition**: past events \(s \to r\) in the same layer;
- **reciprocity**: past events \(r \to s\) in the same layer
  (`reciprocity_count`);
- **sender activity** and **receiver popularity**: the sender's past outgoing
  and the receiver's past incoming events in the same layer
  (`sender_outdegree`, `receiver_indegree`);
- **other layer, same direction** and **other layer, reverse**: past events
  \(s \to r\) and \(r \to s\) in the other layer;
- **same gender**: both students have a recorded gender and it is the same;
  **gender unknown**: at least one gender is missing (the reference is a pair
  of known, different genders).

`endogenous_features()` computes the within-layer statistics against the full
log of the layer (`history_log`). Repetition and the cross-layer counts are
counts of a pair's past events in a given log, built here with one sort:

```{r stats}
# number of events of pair (s -> r) in `log` strictly before each query time
past_count <- function(s, r, t, log) {
  q <- data.frame(k = paste(s, r), t = t, is_log = 0L, id = seq_along(t))
  l <- data.frame(k = paste(log$sender, log$receiver), t = log$time, is_log = 1L, id = NA)
  a <- rbind(q, l)
  a <- a[order(a$k, a$t, a$is_log), ]          # at equal times the query comes first
  before <- ave(a$is_log, a$k, FUN = cumsum)
  out <- integer(length(t)); out[a$id[a$is_log == 0L]] <- before[a$is_log == 0L]
  out
}
add_stats <- function(cc, own, other) {
  cc <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = c("reciprocity_count", "sender_outdegree",
                                          "receiver_indegree"), history_log = own)
  cc$repetition   <- past_count(cc$sender, cc$receiver, cc$time, own)
  cc$cross_same   <- past_count(cc$sender, cc$receiver, cc$time, other)
  cc$cross_rev    <- past_count(cc$receiver, cc$sender, cc$time, other)
  for (v in c("repetition", "reciprocity_count", "sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree",
              "cross_same", "cross_rev")) {
    x <- cc[[v]]; x[is.na(x)] <- 0; cc[[paste0("l_", v)]] <- log1p(x)
  }
  gs <- fem[cc$sender]; gr <- fem[cc$receiver]
  cc$gender_unknown <- as.integer(is.na(gs) | is.na(gr))
  cc$same_gender    <- as.integer(!is.na(gs) & !is.na(gr) & gs == gr)
  cc
}
cc_call <- add_stats(cc_call, own = calls, other = sms)
cc_sms  <- add_stats(cc_sms,  own = sms,   other = calls)
round(rbind(
  calls = tapply(cc_call$cross_same > 0, cc_call$event, mean),
  texts = tapply(cc_sms$cross_same > 0, cc_sms$event, mean)), 3)   # share with past contact in the other layer: controls (0), events (1)
```

```{r cross-numbers, include = FALSE}
cx_c <- tapply(cc_call$cross_same > 0, cc_call$event, mean)
cx_s <- tapply(cc_sms$cross_same > 0, cc_sms$event, mean)
```

`r pct(cx_c[["1"]])` of calls go from a student who had already texted the
callee, against `r pct(cx_c[["0"]], 2)` of the sampled non-events;
`r pct(cx_s[["1"]])` of the sampled text messages follow an earlier call in the
same direction, against `r pct(cx_s[["0"]], 2)` of their non-events.

## Conditional logistic models

The same specification is fitted to each layer with `rem(method = "clogit")`.

```{r clogit}
f <- event ~ l_repetition + l_reciprocity_count + l_sender_outdegree +
  l_receiver_indegree + l_cross_same + l_cross_rev + same_gender + gender_unknown
fit_call <- rem(f, data = cc_call, method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")
fit_sms  <- rem(f, data = cc_sms,  method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")
tab <- function(fit) { s <- summary(fit)$coefficients; s[, c("coef", "se(coef)")] }
round(cbind(calls = tab(fit_call), texts = tab(fit_sms)), 3)
```

```{r forest-figure, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "Coefficients of the call model and the text-message model with 95% intervals, term by term"}
labels <- c(l_repetition = "repetition (same layer)", l_reciprocity_count = "reciprocity (same layer)",
            l_sender_outdegree = "sender activity", l_receiver_indegree = "receiver popularity",
            l_cross_same = "other layer, same direction", l_cross_rev = "other layer, reverse",
            same_gender = "same gender", gender_unknown = "gender unknown")
forest2 <- function(fits, cols, labels) {
  # count terms enter as log(1 + count): one earlier event against none is a step of log(2)
  step <- ifelse(grepl("^l_", names(labels)), log(2), 1)
  b <- sapply(fits, function(f) tab(f)[names(labels), 1]) * step
  s <- sapply(fits, function(f) tab(f)[names(labels), 2]) * step
  k <- nrow(b); y <- k:1; off <- c(0.17, -0.17)
  lo <- b - 1.96 * s; hi <- b + 1.96 * s
  par(mar = c(3.8, 13, 3, 9))
  plot(NA, xlim = range(lo, hi, 0), ylim = c(0.5, k + 0.5), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  rect(par("usr")[1], y[c(TRUE, FALSE)] - 0.5, par("usr")[2], y[c(TRUE, FALSE)] + 0.5, col = "#F6F7F8", border = NA)
  abline(v = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.4)
  abline(v = 0, col = "#AEB5BA", lwd = 1.4)
  for (m in seq_along(fits)) {
    clear <- lo[, m] > 0 | hi[, m] < 0          # interval excludes x1
    segments(lo[, m], y + off[m], hi[, m], y + off[m], col = cols[m], lwd = 3.4)
    points(b[, m], y + off[m], pch = 21, bg = ifelse(clear, cols[m], "white"), col = cols[m], cex = 1.7, lwd = 1.8)
    big <- which(b[, m] >= log(2))
    lab <- paste0("\u00d7", ifelse(exp(b[, m]) >= 10, sprintf("%.0f", exp(b[, m])), sprintf("%.1f", exp(b[, m]))))
    lab[1] <- paste(names(fits)[m], lab[1])
    show <- union(union(1, big), match(c("receiver popularity", "same gender"), labels))
    text(hi[show, m], y[show] + off[m], lab[show], pos = 4, cex = 0.7, col = cols[m], offset = 0.35, xpd = TRUE)
  }
  fac <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50); fac <- fac[log(fac) >= par("usr")[1] & log(fac) <= par("usr")[2]]
  axis(1, at = log(fac), labels = paste0("\u00d7", fac), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.78, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.78, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)
  mtext("rate ratio: one earlier event against none (counts), or the pair having the attribute",
        side = 1, line = 2.2, cex = 0.72, col = ink_soft)
  legend("bottomright", legend = c("interval excludes \u00d71", "interval includes \u00d71"), pch = 21,
         pt.bg = c(ink_soft, "white"), col = ink_soft, pt.cex = 1.4, bty = "n", cex = 0.75, text.col = ink)
}
forest2(list(calls = fit_call, `text messages` = fit_sms), pal[1:2], labels)
title_left("What raises the rate of a call and of a text message",
           "conditional logistic models, one per layer, same statistics; 95% intervals")
```

```{r clogit-numbers, include = FALSE}
bc <- tab(fit_call); bs <- tab(fit_sms)
one <- function(b, v) exp(b[v, 1] * log(2))                 # one earlier event against none
ci1 <- function(b, v) exp((b[v, 1] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * b[v, 2]) * log(2))
ind <- function(b, v) exp(b[v, 1]); ciI <- function(b, v) exp(b[v, 1] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * b[v, 2])
rng <- function(x) paste0(fmt(x[1], 2), " to ", fmt(x[2], 2))
ev_c <- cc_call[cc_call$event == 1, ]; ev_s <- cc_sms[cc_sms$event == 1, ]
r_rep_cross <- c(cor(ev_c$l_repetition, ev_c$l_cross_same), cor(ev_s$l_repetition, ev_s$l_cross_same))
```

Each count enters as \(\log(1 + \text{count})\), so a coefficient \(\beta\) means
that one earlier event against none, and every further doubling of
\(1 + \text{count}\), multiplies the rate by \(2^\beta\). Every effect is
conditional on the others in the same model.

- **History in the other layer.** One earlier text \(s \to r\) multiplies the
  rate of a call \(s \to r\) by `r fmt(one(bc, "l_cross_same"), 1)` (95%
  interval `r rng(ci1(bc, "l_cross_same"))`) once the pair's call history is
  known; one earlier text \(r \to s\) by `r fmt(one(bc, "l_cross_rev"), 1)`
  (`r rng(ci1(bc, "l_cross_rev"))`). For text messages, one earlier call in the
  same direction multiplies the rate by `r fmt(one(bs, "l_cross_same"), 1)`
  (`r rng(ci1(bs, "l_cross_same"))`) and one in the reverse direction by
  `r fmt(one(bs, "l_cross_rev"), 1)` (`r rng(ci1(bs, "l_cross_rev"))`).
- **Within the layer.** One earlier event in the same direction multiplies the
  call rate by `r fmt(one(bc, "l_repetition"), 0)` and the text rate by
  `r fmt(one(bs, "l_repetition"), 0)`; one earlier event in the reverse
  direction by `r fmt(one(bc, "l_reciprocity_count"), 0)` and
  `r fmt(one(bs, "l_reciprocity_count"), 1)`. Against controls drawn
  uniformly from all pairs, almost none of which has any history, these are
  the largest effects in both models.
- **Gender.** A same-gender pair has `r fmt(ind(bc, "same_gender"), 2)` times
  the call rate of a mixed-gender pair with the same history
  (`r rng(ciI(bc, "same_gender"))`); for text messages the factor is
  `r fmt(ind(bs, "same_gender"), 2)` (`r rng(ciI(bs, "same_gender"))`), an
  interval that includes 1.

Among the events, the log count of the pair's past events in its own layer and
in the other layer have correlation `r fmt(r_rep_cross[1], 2)` for calls and
`r fmt(r_rep_cross[2], 2)` for text messages, so the cross-layer coefficients
measure what the other layer adds once the pair's history in the layer is
known.

## The daily cycle as a global covariate

Hour of day and day of the study week take the same value for every pair at a
given instant, so ordinary case-control sampling cannot estimate them (the
event and its controls share the event's time). Time-shifted sampling
(`shift = "exponential"`, `window = c(0, 28)`) gives each control its own time;
the hour and the day of the study week then enter as cyclic smooths in
`rem(method = "gam")`, next to the within-layer and cross-layer counts
(evaluated at each row's own time).

```{r shifted}
shifted <- function(log, own, other, seed) {
  cc <- sample_non_events(log, n_controls = 1, seed = seed, shift = "exponential", window = c(0, 28))
  cc <- add_stats(cc, own, other)
  cc$hour <- (cc$time %% 1) * 24
  cc$wday <- cc$time %% 7
  widen_case_control(cc, covariates = c("hour", "wday", "l_repetition", "l_reciprocity_count",
                                        "l_cross_same", "same_gender", "gender_unknown"))
}
w_call <- shifted(calls[, c("sender", "receiver", "time")], calls, sms, seed = 2)
w_sms  <- shifted(sms_cases, sms, calls, seed = 2)
fg <- ~ nl(hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) + nl(wday, bs = "cc", k = 6) + l_repetition +
  l_reciprocity_count + l_cross_same + same_gender + gender_unknown
g_call <- rem(fg, data = w_call, method = "gam")
g_sms  <- rem(fg, data = w_sms,  method = "gam")
rbind(calls = summary(g_call)$s.table[, "p-value"], texts = summary(g_sms)$s.table[, "p-value"])
```

```{r cycle-figure, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Estimated effect of the hour of day on the rate of calls and of text messages, with 95% bands"}
dh_c <- smooth_data(g_call$fit, 1); dh_s <- smooth_data(g_sms$fit, 1)
yl <- range(dh_c$fit - 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_c$fit + 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_s$fit - 1.96 * dh_s$se, dh_s$fit + 1.96 * dh_s$se)
par(mar = c(3.6, 4.2, 3, 7))
band <- function(d, col) {
  lo <- d$fit - 1.96 * d$se; hi <- d$fit + 1.96 * d$se
  polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = alpha(col, 0.12), border = NA)
  lines(d$x, lo, col = alpha(col, 0.6), lwd = 0.8, lty = 3); lines(d$x, hi, col = alpha(col, 0.6), lwd = 0.8, lty = 3)
}
plot(dh_c$x, dh_c$fit, type = "n", ylim = yl, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", xlim = c(0, 24))
abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
band(dh_c, pal[1]); band(dh_s, pal[2])
lines(dh_c$x, dh_c$fit, col = pal[1], lwd = 2.4); lines(dh_s$x, dh_s$fit, col = pal[2], lwd = 2.4)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 24, 3), labels = sprintf("%02d:00", seq(0, 24, 3)), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("time of day, if the study day starts at midnight", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
mtext("effect on the log-rate", side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
n <- nrow(dh_c)
text(24, dh_c$fit[n] - 0.08, "calls", pos = 4, col = pal[1], cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE)
text(24, dh_s$fit[n] + 0.08, "text messages", pos = 4, col = pal[2], cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE)
# trough-to-peak bracket for calls
xt <- dh_c$x[which.min(dh_c$fit)]; xp <- dh_c$x[which.max(dh_c$fit)]
arrows(xp + 1.6, min(dh_c$fit), xp + 1.6, max(dh_c$fit), code = 3, length = 0.05, angle = 90, col = ink, lwd = 1)
segments(xt, min(dh_c$fit), xp + 1.6, min(dh_c$fit), col = alpha(ink, 0.35), lty = 2)
text(xp + 1.9, mean(range(dh_c$fit)), sprintf("peak / trough:\n%s\u00d7 for calls\n%s\u00d7 for texts", fmt(exp(diff(range(dh_c$fit))), 0), fmt(exp(diff(range(dh_s$fit))), 0)),
     adj = 0, cex = 0.68, col = ink, xpd = TRUE)
title_left("A similar daily cycle in both channels",
           "effect of the time of day on the log-rate (cyclic smooth, dotted lines: 95% band), next to the history terms")
```

```{r cycle-numbers, include = FALSE}
amp <- function(d) diff(range(d$fit))
lowh <- function(d) d$x[which.min(d$fit)]; highh <- function(d) d$x[which.max(d$fit)]
```

On the log-rate scale the hour-of-day effect spans
`r fmt(amp(dh_c), 1)` for calls and `r fmt(amp(dh_s), 1)` for text messages:
a factor of `r fmt(exp(amp(dh_c)), 0)` and `r fmt(exp(amp(dh_s)), 0)` between
the quietest hour (around `r fmt(lowh(dh_c), 0)`:00 for calls,
`r fmt(lowh(dh_s), 0)`:00 for texts) and the busiest (around
`r fmt(highh(dh_c), 0)`:00 and `r fmt(highh(dh_s), 0)`:00). The two curves
have a similar shape; their 95% bands overlap at
`r ov <- mean(pmin(dh_c$fit + 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_s$fit + 1.96 * dh_s$se) > pmax(dh_c$fit - 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_s$fit - 1.96 * dh_s$se)); if (ov == 1) "every hour" else paste(pct(ov, 0), "of the hours")`,
and the call curve lies above the text curve
around midday. The day of the
study week adds no effect that the data separate from zero (p
`r pfmt(summary(g_call)$s.table[2, "p-value"])` for calls,
p `r pfmt(summary(g_sms)$s.table[2, "p-value"])` for text messages): its
smooth is shrunk to a flat line in both models.

## What the data cannot say

- The release gives elapsed time only. Hour of day assumes a midnight start,
  and the weekly cycle has no weekday names.
- Calls include missed calls; a model of answered calls only would drop the
  `r pct(missed)` with duration `-1`.
- The text-message model uses 3,600 of the 24,333 messages as cases (fixed
  seed); its standard errors are larger than a model on all messages would
  give.
- Phones record only communication between participants; calls and texts to
  people outside the study are not in the logs.

## Reference

Sapiezynski P, Stopczynski A, Lassen DD, Lehmann S (2019). Interaction data
from the Copenhagen Networks Study. *Scientific Data* 6, 315.
doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0325-x.
